picks.name: Perfect Blue
picks.why: Satoshi Kon's animated psychological thriller follows a pop idol turned actress who is stalked by a doppelgänger of her old self, as the role she plays seeps into her real life. It is tightly controlled, frightening, and leaves a puzzle to piece together afterward.

picks.name: The Prestige
picks.why: Two rival stage magicians wreck each other's lives chasing the perfect illusion. It's a film about doubles and performers who live their act for real, and its final reveal changes everything before it.

picks.name: The Game
picks.why: Fincher's paranoid thriller about a rich man pulled into a staged 'game' that may be a con, a murder plot or both. Everyone around him might be an actor, and the screws tighten all the way to the end.

picks.name: Arlington Road
picks.why: A widower comes to suspect that his friendly new neighbors are not who they seem. A tight paranoid thriller with one of the most merciless endings of its decade.

picks.name: Juror #2
picks.why: An ordinary man on a murder jury realizes he may be responsible for the death being tried and calmly weighs whether to let someone else pay. A taut moral thriller with a cold, precise finish.

picks.name: A Talent for Murder
picks.why: A mysterious young man is sent to persuade Patricia Highsmith to write one last Ripley novel. It's a cat-and-mouse game about performance, impostors and fiction leaking into real life.

picks.name: Incendies
picks.why: Villeneuve's mystery follows twins who trace their dead mother's past through a war-torn country. It tightens steadily toward one of the most devastating final reveals in modern film.

picks.name: Decision to Leave
picks.why: Park Chan-wook's noir about a detective who falls for the widow he suspects of murder. It is precise and full of misdirection, and the ending stays with you long after it's over.

picks.name: One Hour Photo
picks.why: Robin Williams plays a lonely photo-lab clerk whose quiet fixation on a family turns menacing. It's a calm, unsettling portrait of an ordinary man sliding toward something monstrous.

picks.name: Gentle Monster
picks.why: Marie Kreutzer's thriller about a renowned pianist who moves her family to the countryside and uncovers a shattering truth. It's a tense study of deception inside a marriage.

new.name: Heartland
new.why: A reclusive former country star comes out of hiding to look for her missing niece in Nashville and uncovers dark secrets tied to her own past. A missing-person mystery where every lead points back to the family.

new.name: A Story of Derry
new.why: Three youngsters enter the Western Wood centuries before Pennywise and meet an ancient evil. Folk horror built on fear rather than spectacle.

new.name: Silent Night, Deadly Night
new.why: A man who watched his parents murdered by someone in a Santa suit puts one on to take revenge. A grim, pulpy holiday slasher with a revenge spine.

new.name: The End of Oak Street
new.why: A cosmic event drops a suburban street somewhere unknown, and the neighbors' civility starts to fray. A mystery about ordinary people under pressure.

new.name: I Was a Stranger
new.why: Five strangers' lives collide on one night when survival is uncertain. A tense, interlocking drama.

new.name: Pressure
new.why: Eisenhower and his meteorologist face an impossible go or no-go call in the 72 hours before D-Day. A controlled pressure-cooker thriller.

new.name: The Dog Stars
new.why: A pilot who survived a pandemic guards his small patch of land against scavengers. A spare post-apocalyptic thriller about what survivors become.

new.name: The Furious
new.why: A father goes to war with the ruthless kidnappers who took his daughter. A hard-edged action thriller.

new.name: The Mongoose
new.why: A decorated combat veteran is fleeing a murder scene at 130 miles an hour. Pure propulsive pulp.

new.name: Fjord
new.why: Cristian Mungiu sets a Romanian immigrant family in Norway against a child-welfare investigation. The precise, slow-tightening drama turns the scrutiny of decent institutions into something quietly menacing.

dread.name: The Invitation
dread.why: At a dinner party in his ex-wife's house, a man grows sure that the hosts are planning something. The dread builds slowly to a terrific final shot.

dread.name: 10 Cloverfield Lane
dread.why: A woman wakes up in a survivalist's bunker and is told that the world outside is gone. A tense captivity thriller with a captor who is calm, polite and frightening.

dread.name: The Tenant
dread.why: Polanski's man moves into a flat where the last tenant tried to kill herself, and slowly turns into her. A creeping study of identity loss.

dread.name: Martha Marcy May Marlene
dread.why: A young woman who has escaped a cult can't tell her old life from the one she ran from. Quietly devastating, with a final scene that leaves the threat open.

dread.name: Audition
dread.why: A widower stages a fake film audition to find a new wife and picks the wrong woman. A slow, calm romance that turns into pure horror.

dread.name: The Invisible Guest
dread.why: A businessman accused of his lover's murder has one night to build his defense with a top lawyer. A Spanish thriller full of twists, and every one is earned.

dread.name: The Secret in Their Eyes
dread.why: A retired investigator reopens a brutal murder case that never left him. The Argentine thriller's final revelation hits hard.

dread.name: The Wicker Man
dread.why: A devout policeman searches a pagan island for a missing girl while the islanders politely play along. One of the great endings in horror.

dread.name: Blow Out
dread.why: A movie sound man records evidence of a political murder and can't make anyone listen. De Palma at his most controlled, with a gut-punch finale.

dread.name: The Pledge
dread.why: A retiring detective swears to a grieving mother that he'll catch her child's killer, and the vow consumes him. Sean Penn directs a slow, tightening obsession with a bitterly ironic ending.

deadpan.name: The Man Who Wasn't There
deadpan.why: A taciturn barber's blackmail scheme leads to murder and he barely blinks. The Coens' deadpan noir in black and white.

deadpan.name: Bad Education
deadpan.why: A beloved school superintendent is quietly at the center of a massive embezzlement scandal. True-life fraud played with a straight face, and Hugh Jackman never drops the act.

deadpan.name: Killer Joe
deadpan.why: A broke family hires a cop who moonlights as a hitman, and offers their daughter as his retainer. A vicious Southern noir comedy with a notorious finale.

deadpan.name: Swimming with Sharks
deadpan.why: A Hollywood assistant takes his abusive studio boss hostage. A bitter satire that ends with a cold twist.

deadpan.name: American Psycho
deadpan.why: A Wall Street yuppie confesses his murders to people who can't tell him apart from anyone else. A satire of masks and conformity played completely straight.

deadpan.name: Calvary
deadpan.why: In confession, a priest is told he will be killed in a week for another man's sins. Bleak Irish gallows humor building to a reckoning.

deadpan.name: Riders of Justice
deadpan.why: A grieving soldier and a trio of statistics nerds calmly set out to avenge a train crash. A Danish revenge comedy, darker and stranger than it sounds.

deadpan.name: In Order of Disappearance
deadpan.why: A stoic snowplow driver works through a drug gang to avenge his son. Norwegian deadpan, with the body count kept like a ledger.

deadpan.name: The Banshees of Inisherin
deadpan.why: On a remote Irish island, one man abruptly ends a friendship and backs it up with a horrifying threat that he fully means. The comedy is bleak and deadpan, and the pettiness escalates into self-mutilation and arson.

deadpan.name: The Player
deadpan.why: A studio executive kills a writer he wrongly thinks has been threatening him, and Hollywood barely notices. Altman's satire plays it completely straight, and the ending is perfectly cynical.

deepcuts.name: With a Friend Like Harry...
deepcuts.why: A vacationing family man meets an old schoolmate who decides to 'help' his life by any means necessary. A French thriller with a calm, smiling menace.

deepcuts.name: Elena
deepcuts.why: A quiet former nurse married to a wealthy man makes a calm, terrible decision for her own family. Zvyagintsev's precise moral thriller.

deepcuts.name: Lake Mungo
deepcuts.why: An Australian mock-documentary about a drowned girl whose grieving family keep finding her double in photos. A quiet, deeply unsettling puzzle.

deepcuts.name: Wake in Fright
deepcuts.why: A schoolteacher stranded in an outback mining town is swallowed by its friendly, drunken brutality. Ordinary men at their worst.

deepcuts.name: Hatching
deepcuts.why: A Finnish girl pressured by her perfectionist mother hatches a creature that becomes her monstrous double. Doppelgänger body horror.

deepcuts.name: The Innocents
deepcuts.why: Children on a Norwegian housing estate discover powers, and one uses them with escalating cruelty. A quiet film of real terror.

deepcuts.name: Andhadhun
deepcuts.why: A pianist who fakes blindness witnesses a murder he supposedly can't see. A darkly comic Indian thriller about a performance with deadly consequences.

deepcuts.name: Nine Queens
deepcuts.why: Two Buenos Aires con men chase one big score with a sheet of forged stamps. A slippery puzzle in which everyone is playing a role.

deepcuts.name: The Servant
deepcuts.why: A wealthy young Londoner's manservant slowly reverses their roles and takes control. A cold, insidious power-game drama.

deepcuts.name: Knife in the Water
deepcuts.why: A couple picks up a hitchhiker for a sailing weekend, and male rivalry turns dangerous. Polanski's tight three-hander debut.

doubles.name: Us
doubles.why: A family on a beach vacation is attacked by their own doppelgängers, and the horror grows into a twisted allegory about who gets to live which life. The final reveal changes everything that came before.

doubles.name: Mulholland Drive
doubles.why: An aspiring actress and an amnesiac woman try to work out the amnesiac's identity in Los Angeles, until their roles invert and the dream sours. It's David Lynch's ultimate puzzle film about performance and stolen identity.

doubles.name: Lost Highway
doubles.why: A jazz saxophonist accused of murdering his wife inexplicably turns into another man entirely. Lynch's noir about split identities runs on dread, and its loop structure begs to be decoded.

doubles.name: Triangle
doubles.why: Yachting friends board a deserted ocean liner, and one woman begins running into versions of herself. It's a tightly plotted loop thriller where each double reveals something worse.

doubles.name: Possession
doubles.why: A Berlin marriage disintegrates, and the husband finds a calm, angelic double of his wife while she spirals into something monstrous. Andrzej Żuławski's ferocious film is unlike anything else.

doubles.name: Shattered Glass
doubles.why: A charming young journalist at The New Republic turns out to have invented dozens of his stories. The film is a gripping true account of a compulsive impostor whose performance collapses one fact-check at a time.

doubles.name: Black Swan
doubles.why: A ballerina cast as both the White and the Black Swan is consumed by the role and by a rival who seems to be her dark double. Darren Aronofsky's psychological horror is about performance swallowing a person.

doubles.name: Moon
doubles.why: Near the end of a three-year solo contract on a lunar mining base, a worker meets a man who is exactly him. It's a quiet, tense sci-fi mystery about identity and corporate cruelty.

doubles.name: Changeling
doubles.why: In 1928 Los Angeles, police return a mother's missing son, and she insists the boy is not him. Clint Eastwood's true-story thriller is an impostor case wrapped in institutional cruelty.

doubles.name: The Spanish Prisoner
doubles.why: An inventor with a valuable secret is lured into an elaborate con in which everyone around him may be playing a part. David Mamet's precise puzzle-box thriller keeps pulling the rug away.

series.name: Severance
series.why: Office workers surgically split their work selves from their home selves, and the doubles start to rebel. Precise, eerie, and every episode ends on a hook.

series.name: Barry
series.why: A hitman takes up acting, and his roles and his murders start to bleed together. Pitch-black comedy that grows darker every season.

series.name: Mousetrap
series.why: A reclusive writer wakes up to find a man called The Rat living his life, and allies with a loan shark to get it back. An identity-theft thriller.

series.name: The Outsider
series.why: A beloved coach is arrested for a child's murder despite proof that he was elsewhere, and a double is at work. Grim, slow-burn horror procedural.

series.name: Inside No. 9
series.why: A British anthology of half-hour dark tales, each with a vicious final twist. Deadpan, cruel and very bingeable.

series.name: Dark Matter
series.why: A physicist is abducted into an alternate version of his life while his double takes over his family. A doppelgänger thriller with momentum.

series.name: Hannibal
series.why: An FBI profiler and his psychiatrist, secretly a cannibal, are locked in an elegant battle of minds. Stylish, cruel and precise.

series.name: The Americans
series.why: Two Soviet spies live as an ordinary suburban couple in 1980s Washington, playing their roles so well that the false life and the real one become impossible to separate. Every season raises the stakes, and the series finale is one of television's most devastating.
